paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: We show the empirical generalization errors (termed Error in the figures) and estimated Hessian traces of the loss for fine-tuned adapters (using QAdapter on Llama-3-8B) across various hidden dimensions. Smaller adapters achieve the lowest generalization errors. Additionally, the Hessian trace values correlate with generalization errors, suggesting that smaller adapters tend to converge to flatter minima.

The y-axis is unlabeled and uses a linear scale with visible tick labels at 0.3, 0.6, and 0.9, spanning approximately from about 0.25 up to about 1.0. One line is shown: a solid black line connecting large green circular markers (each marker has a vertical black error bar with horizontal caps). The series starts near 0.34 at rank 4, decreases slightly to about 0.32 at rank 16, increases to about 0.41 at rank 64, and increases further to about 0.63 at rank 256, with the largest displayed y-value occurring at rank 256; the error bars are shortest around ranks 4–16 and appear larger at ranks 64 and 256.
